archetypes.name: launcher-contract
archetypes.rationale: The waterfall's Codex/Cursor tiers pass flags to launch-review.sh that may not exist there; the Claude tier's tool-capable claim rests on --help output alone, not verified runtime Read-tool access in --print mode.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check that every flag the plan proposes passing to launch-review.sh for the Codex/Cursor tiers (--mode, --timing-task-kind, --diff-file, --scope-files, --plan-file) is actually parsed and accepted by that script — find its flag-parsing block and confirm each flag name. Separately verify that claude --print combined with --add-dir and --allowedTools actually grants Read tool access to the subprocess in headless mode rather than merely accepting those flags syntactically; look for any --permission-mode or --no-tools default that would silently suppress tool scaffolding. If launch-review.sh validates or enumerates recognized timing-task-kind values, confirm 'scout-dynamic-archetypes' would not be rejected as an unknown kind. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: env-threading
archetypes.rationale: The plan uses SESSION_ROOT in the Claude tier and CODEX_AVAILABLE/CURSOR_AVAILABLE across three callers, but these variable names must match what each script actually exports in its execution context, or the waterfall silently degrades to Claude-only.
archetypes.prompt_body: Confirm that SESSION_ROOT (or whatever scout-dynamic-archetypes.sh calls the session tmpdir) is actually defined and exported in that script's execution context; if the name differs, the --add-dir path for the Claude tool-capable tier would be wrong or empty. Trace the presence variables (CODEX_AVAILABLE, CURSOR_AVAILABLE, or however they are named) from dispatch-panel.sh and plan-review-loop.sh through each scout wrapper invocation, checking for any name mismatch, missing export, or unset default that would leave the waterfall in Claude-only mode even when Codex or Cursor are present. Verify that SCOUT_DYNAMIC_ARCHETYPES_LAUNCH_SH override is scoped only to the Claude tier and does not suppress the Codex/Cursor tiers when set, since the plan says to keep its override semantics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: diff-exclusion-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds the larch-logs exclusion only in gather-branch-context.sh, but the 855 KB bloat came from an implement review — the plan should confirm this is the single diff-build point for the affected code path and that no other pipeline legs also accumulate run-log artifacts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Locate every place in the review pipeline (both /implement and /design modes) that builds a git diff destined for the scout or reviewer prompts, not just gather-branch-context.sh, and check whether each would still pick up larch-logs artifacts after the single-file change the plan proposes. Check whether /design code-review mode (which the plan says does not use gather-branch-context.sh) builds its own diff elsewhere, and if so whether that path also needs the exclusion. Verify that the pathspec ':(exclude)larch-logs/**' is syntactically valid for the git version used in CI and does not accidentally exclude other paths that merely share a larch-logs prefix. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
